headline: Software Surge Leads a Split Session as Breadth Stays Negative
body_html:
Thursday's midday tape is telling a tale of two markets. Software names are commanding the session's narrative, with the sector up more than three percent and cybersecurity names posting some of the sharpest single-day moves in recent memory. Okta is leading all comers with a gain approaching thirty percent, followed by Salesforce at nearly twenty-four percent and CrowdStrike north of twenty — a triumvirate of enterprise-software strength that is pulling the broader technology complex higher even as the rest of the market struggles to keep pace.

Beneath that headline glow, breadth is decidedly negative: 304 names in our universe are declining against 241 advancing, out of 549 tracked. Energy is the session's second-best sector, gaining 1.8%, aided by elevated crude prices tied to the ongoing Iran conflict. Semiconductors are modestly positive at just over one percent. On the other side of the ledger, Homebuilders are the worst performers, off nearly 1.5%, with Consumer and Industrials also in the red.

Into the close, traders will be watching whether software gains hold without broader participation. Any remarks from Fed Governor Warsh — which prediction markets are already pricing for market impact — could shift tone in the final hour.

briefs.headline: Okta Rockets to Session High After Earnings Catalyst
briefs.body: Identity-security provider Okta is the standout mover of the day, surging nearly thirty percent mid-session in what amounts to one of the largest single-day advances in the software space this year. The move is drawing broad attention to the identity-management segment and lifting sentiment across enterprise software peers.

briefs.headline: Iran Conflict's Sixth-Month Mark Weighs on Energy Policy Calculus
briefs.body: Reporting characterizes the Iran war as having reached a costly stalemate after six months of fighting, even as the conflict continues to pressure fuel prices. President Trump is set to convene meetings with refiners and fuel retailers amid rising gas costs that carry political sensitivity ahead of the midterm cycle.

briefs.headline: Warsh Comments Put Fixed-Income Traders on Alert
briefs.body: Prediction markets are actively handicapping the likely content and market impact of remarks expected from Fed Governor Kevin Warsh, adding an event-risk dimension to Thursday afternoon trading. Kansas City Fed President Schmid separately described inflation as 'stubborn' and 'sticky,' suggesting the policy rate remains a live debate within the central bank.

briefs.headline: Burlington and Tapestry Drag Retail Lower as Consumer Sector Slips
briefs.body: Burlington Stores is off more than seven percent mid-session, while luxury-apparel name Tapestry has dropped nearly five and a half percent, underscoring the Consumer sector's 0.98% decline on the day. The moves reflect continued pressure on discretionary spending names even as technology commands investor attention.

briefs.headline: Visa and Mastercard Open Card Rails Into Syria After US Policy Shift
briefs.body: Both payments networks announced the launch of international card transaction services in Syria following the United States' removal of the country's terrorism designation. The move marks a significant expansion of the global payments infrastructure into a market that had been closed to Western financial networks for years.

briefs.headline: Family Offices Leaning Bullish Despite Uneven Market Internals
briefs.body: Survey data tracked by CNBC's Family Office Portfolio Tracker shows wealthy multi-generational investors are making an affirmative bet on equities even as today's breadth figures — more decliners than advancers — highlight the session's mixed underlying character. The positioning suggests conviction in longer-duration risk assets among sophisticated allocators.
